stats.title: How to Pose Like A Classy Lady in Photos

structure.what_is_said: "Have you ever noticed how some women look so natural and elegant in photos? And then the second a camera is pointed at us, we suddenly do not know what to do with ourselves?" Where to put hands, how to stand, whether to smile. "Usually the women who look the most effortless in photos are not actually posing perfectly. They just understand a few small details that make everything look softer, more natural, and more elegant."

structure.how_it_is_shown: White card "1. Solo Photos" in black script

structure.what_is_said: Lighting (soft, balanced is most flattering; harsh light or angles change a photo; "Why do I look like that?" - studies say people look more attractive in real life). Solo photos: posture (stand tall, relax shoulders, avoid facing the camera straight on; angle body, shift weight, one foot forward); hands (touch hair, hold bag, rest near waist).
structure.how_it_is_shown: Cinematic FULL clips, 2 halves, same-woman 2-photo comparison on white, stock FULL clip, FULL reels, ROW(3), ROW(2)+caramel text panel (tip lines), half photo + caramel text, 3 separated photos on white built one per second

structure.what_is_said: "Group photos can sometimes"
structure.how_it_is_shown: White card "2. Group Photos" written on

structure.what_is_said: Group photos: don't stand stiff or separated; slight lean, relaxed stance, interact; with a close friend/partner lean in or rest a hand on their arm or leg; on the end angle inward; in the middle one foot forward; expression relaxed, soft smile, eye contact with the person beside you, candid mid-conversation; "The goal is not to look perfectly posed together. It is to look comfortable within the moment."
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL group reel 6.5 s; 2-half and 3-panel rows; separated photos on white; single centred photos on white for each group rule (2:34, 2:38, 2:43); caramel + square centred photos; FULL reels

structure.what_is_said: "When you are standing in a photo,"
structure.how_it_is_shown: White card "3. Standing Photos"

structure.what_is_said: Shift weight to one side, one foot forward, cross ankles; slight lean; stand tall with relaxed shoulders; hands soft and lightly engaged (fingers together, near waist, hold a small bag or glass); soft smile and eye contact with the camera.
structure.how_it_is_shown: Rows built centre-first and left-to-right, single centred photo on white, half photo + caramel quote with script words, separated photos on white, one FULL reel held 9 s for the expression tip

structure.what_is_said: Sit tall but soft; angle body to the side; rest elbow, hand near face; hands natural; holding a drink: wine by the stem, cup by the handle.

structure.what_is_said: Little movements: tuck hair behind ear, chin on hand; "The best sitting photos usually feel like you are simply enjoying the moment, not thinking too much about the camera."
structure.how_it_is_shown: ROW(3) built; half photo + caramel quote card

structure.what_is_said: "And for candid photos,"
structure.how_it_is_shown: White card "5. Candid Photos"

structure.what_is_said: Candid photos are just movement: adjusting a heel, fixing a bag, touching hair, slow steps; walking photos; the best photos happen between poses (laughing, looking away); "The less you try to pose perfectly, the more natural and elegant the photo starts to feel."
structure.how_it_is_shown: Separated photos on white, ROW(3)s, caramel + 2 panels built on the words, walking reel in a row centre, 4 FULL reel shots (6:15-6:26), half photo + caramel quote

structure.what_is_said: Mirror photos: don't stand straight; angle, weight on one leg, foot forward; one hand on hip, in pocket or holding the bag; phone in front of the face to take pressure off the expression and focus on the outfit.

tricks: 1 HOOK (0:00-0:32): a "Have you ever noticed..." question over a FULL clip of an elegant woman; the relatable problem ("the second a camera is pointed at us...") plays over ONE creator reel held 9 s (0:04-0:13) of a woman confidently posing; then the list "where to put our hands, how to stand, whether to smile" gets a caramel single -> 3-panel row of smiling women (0:13-0:19); empty caramel breath (0:19); 2 halves (0:20); two FULL walking clips on "not actually posing perfectly... small details" (0:24-0:32). About 8 picture changes in 32 s (avg 4 s). No text in the hook. Title appears at 0:32.3-0:38.7 on a darkened café clip: "Episode 23" + script "How to Pose Elegantly".

2 POINT OPENING: white card with number + name in black script ("1. Solo Photos" ... "6. Mirror Photos"), 2.8-3.9 s, entered by dissolve (0.5-1.3 s), while the narrator says the name ("Group photos can sometimes...", "When you are standing in a photo,"). Before the card: usually a dissolve from the previous section's last quote card or row; for point 4 an empty caramel frame (4:13). After the card: a long dissolve (2.3 s) into a cinematic clip (point 1), a cut into a FULL group reel (point 2), a cut to caramel+centre (point 3), a caramel fade (point 4), separated photos on white (points 5 and 6).

2b POINT CLOSE: several points close on a half-photo + caramel quote card that sums up the point: standing (3:38-3:45, mid-point), sitting (5:24-5:32), candid (6:26-6:34); group closes on a 2-panel row with "comfortable within the moment" (3:03-3:09).

3 HOLD TIMES: ROW(3) 4-7 s (1:17-1:22.8 = 5.8 s; 4:28-4:35 = 7 s); 2-halves 4-5 s; separated photos on white 4-6 s; tip-text panels 6-12.8 s (6:44-6:56.8); FULL creator reels held long: 0:04-0:13 (9 s, posing), 1:10-1:16 (6 s), 1:49-1:55.8 (6.4 s group), 3:57-4:06 (9 s, soft smile + eye contact demonstrated). Single caramel+centre mirror selfies held 6-7 s (6:58-7:11).

4 ROWS: 3 panels is the norm (machine labels of 4-9 are wrong); always DIFFERENT women except the 7:32 try-on row (one creator in 3 dresses) and 5:35 (likely one creator). Rows are built: centre first then sides (0:13->0:14, 3:12.8->3:14, 3:31->3:32.7, 4:06->4:07.7), or left-to-right one per second on the listed items (1:05-1:06; 1:38/1:39/1:40 on "touch your hair / hold your bag / rest your hand"; 3:18/3:19/3:20; 7:12/7:13). Two-photo rows also build on words: right panel arrives on "taking a few slow steps" (5:54).

4b NEW LAYOUT in this video: photos with WHITE GAPS on a white background (2, 3 or 1 centred) used for "rule" examples (1:37, 2:09, 2:13, 2:34, 2:38, 2:43, 3:25, 3:52, 4:21, 4:49, 4:53, 4:59, 5:35, 5:56, 6:38, 7:11), alternating with edge-to-edge rows on caramel.
5 SMALL TEXT: none apart from the CA watermark and the QR code; no creator credits or @handles anywhere; the wall lettering "THE SUSSEX..." (4:17) and "LE CLUB" (4:43) are in the original photos.

6 NAMED WOMEN: none named. Event photos appear without names: couple at the Wimbledon "The Championships / Emirates" sponsor backdrop (2:53-2:57, half of a 2-panel row) and a couple in Wimbledon stands (2:23-2:27, caramel+centre).

7 DO/DON'T: no marks, ticks or crosses. The only comparison is two photos of the SAME woman side by side on white with no labels on "angles can completely change the way a photo looks" (0:50.8-0:54.6). Do/don't is told in words and in the caramel tip lines ("Avoid facing the camera completely straight on.", "Avoid standing completely straight.").

8 COMMENT ASKS AND GUIDE: (a) mid-video keyword ask at 5:09.7-5:16.6, inside point 4: "comment etiquette below" with text Comment "Etiquette" over 2 darkened FULL clips; (b) guide mention 7:30-7:51 right after the last point, before the conclusion: "you can access our personal stylist guide linked below. It's sent instantly to your email." with text "Check the description for / Personal Stylist Guide / www.classyladyacademy.com" and a QR code; the visuals before it are a one-creator try-on row (colours / what flatters you); (c) end ask for a part two ("comment pose"), "which type of photos do you personally struggle with the most", and "a simple like or comment" - no text. No subscribe ask.

9 ENDING (last 40 s, 7:51-8:30): conclusion over the SAME cinematic Sorrento campaign clips used at the start of point 1 (0:41-0:45) - a bookend; then calm FULL clips with long dissolves (6.7 s at 8:03, 3.8 s at 8:15), no text; "Until next time. Bye, my loves." then 1.4 s dissolve to the white CA logo card held about 10 s; the music swells only there (about -16.5 dB at 8:22-8:23) and fades to silence by 8:28; picture holds 2 s more.

10 OTHER: (a) each spoken micro-instruction gets a photo that shows exactly that action (hand at chin, glass by the stem, cup by the handle, phone in front of face, adjusting a heel); (b) the narrator adds a personal aside on a photo ("Such a pretty dress." 3:29); (c) diversity is deliberate in rows: Black, East Asian, olive, fair, a woman in a headscarf, a plus-size woman and a woman in her 60s; (d) empty caramel frames (about 1 s) are used as breaths between ideas (0:19, 0:50, 2:33, 4:13, 4:36, 4:47, 6:57, 7:24, 7:37); (e) one stock-like clip is used for a literal idea (phone taking a photo, 0:54) and one for the comment ask (5:10).
